# C2 preflight proposal: reproducible edit loops and Windows CI parity

Status: read-only planning, 2026-09-14. No child claim, worktree creation,
Cargo invocation, source touch, review marker or GitHub write was performed.
This scratch plan is not a mission-completion or score report.

Tier: **high**, retained from issue #477. The work changes CI execution and a
measurement/budget contract; reducing the issue's tier to medium would evade
its assigned independent source-first and full delivery obligations.

## Sources inspected before deriving the map

- Issue: https://github.com/milocaetano/quantick/issues/477, body read directly.
- Parent campaign/user constraints retained below; current implementation base
  must be the verified campaign tip after C1 integration, not this planning SHA.
- Canonical `.claude/skills/mission/SKILL.md`, `docs/workflow/delivery.md`,

  `52b1e4362b47c67e8372842a72f1f818ac361967`, workflow delta versus `05bc95ec`.
- Frozen rubric and `tools/outside_score/measure.py`, read without edits.
  A read-only `python -B tools/outside_score/measure.py .` invocation confirmed
  crate production counts at that C1 worktree; it assigns no score.
- Root Cargo/profile and package manifests; existing CI/supply-chain workflows;

Do not reimplement sibling fixes; retain their regressions and run targeted cases if a C2 repair touches those inputs. Supply raw facts to the parent's fresh assessor; do not score this work. |

## Operational gates and closing steps

- G1 (mission/delivery): root independently reconciles full original/delegated
  sources with this map, retaining its exact reviewed revision before code.
- G2 (new-task/integration): only start after C1's campaign merge is reachable
  with required green evidence; new owned branch/worktree from verified
  `origin/campaign/outside-eight`; branch-private high-tier/base markers and
  guard build plus relevant pre-edit check before implementation edits.
- G3 (CLAUDE/delivery): English, existing ratchets and one-way/headless invariants;
  changes classify as rare/offline CI tooling, not market hot-path changes.
  Full ordered fmt/clippy/build/test before code commits; affected Python lint,
  runner fixtures and workflow behavioral checks; exact-head CI on both OSes.
- G4 (mission/arch-review): current independent architecture/bug and AI reviews;
  all required findings resolved with durable reports and zero AI threads.
  Actual mission includes the four literal reserved G-AI lines unchanged.
- G5 (authority): root owns publication journal, campaign integration and
  settings-task placement; trader alone merges main. No settings/API workaround.
- G6 (durable progress): initial operation=0 and repair=0 for this new child;
  retain failed attempts and cumulative counters across sessions under the
  delivery progress contract. Bind issue/Project/branch/worktree/PR/head/base
  and checkpoint identities only after readback; unknown values remain null.
  Evidence destinations are child #477 comments, its current-head PR checks
  and review reports, and parent #472 checkpoints. Root owns these writes.
- C1: high-tier independent delivery review PASS at current review key.
- C2: reviewed, ready child PR with exact-head green CI and evidence links.
- C3: shared mission/ship verifier PASS, return child to root for serialized
  campaign integration; main score and scheduled-default-branch proof are not
  pre-awarded by a child merge.

No UI feature, financial action, capability, crate or hot-path implementation is
proposed. Visual/new-extension/hot-path-change gates are N/A unless scope changes;
historical dense performance evidence cannot substitute for edit-loop evidence.

Preflight revision 2 closes the proposed map's C2-PF1/C2-PF2 traceability gaps
without adding a product outcome or changing R1-R5/A1-A5. Before code, retain
five touched samples and the provisional calibration-headroom rule as explicit
mission assumptions/decisions under the user's delegated defaults. Actual
budget numbers remain unknown until measured on the declared host class.

## Existing commands and exact current target selection

The frozen lexer counts masked nonblank production Rust lines, excluding its
test-file/test-span definitions, grouped by nearest Cargo manifest. It does not
rank by raw file length, test count or compile duration. Recompute at the actual
measurement SHA, sort descending by production lines with crate name tie-break,
and cross-check a same-quantity guard report if available; guard rows win where
the rubric says so. Reject drift/missing candidates rather than substituting.

| Rank at inspected C1 SHA | Frozen production lines | Timed command | Proposed touched production file |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| app | 77,218 | `cargo test -p quantick-app` | `crates/app/src/app.rs` |
| orderflow | 5,045 | `cargo test -p quantick-orderflow` | `crates/orderflow/src/engine.rs` |
| pine | 4,939 | `cargo test -p quantick-pine` | `crates/pine/src/compile.rs` |

These are real compiled central production modules, not test-only/unused tiny
substitutes. The app runner must execute the whole package (binary tests), not
`--lib`, `--no-run`, a test-name filter, `--release`, or a replacement crate.
Manifest package names are the `quantick-*` values, not directory names.

The mandatory full loop is separately:

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
cargo build --workspace
cargo test --workspace
```

Existing Python commands remain `python3 tools/read_cost/test_measure.py`,
`python3 tools/outside_score/test_measure.py`, exporter/bridge suites and
`pipx run ruff check --select F tools/ bridge/mt5/`. A proposed new
`tools/edit_loop/test_measure.py` joins that offline set; its path is a proposal,
not an existing command. Do not change frozen `tools/outside_score/measure.py`.

## Proposed safe measurement protocol

1. Finish/commit the C2 runner/workflow code after required validation. Resolve
   full code SHA H, tree, toolchain/profile/lock hashes and clean state. Create a
   dedicated detached benchmark worktree at H under an explicitly owned sibling
   path after root records its lease. Never touch a writer's current checkout.
2. Keep measurements/logs outside that checkout, then add their raw results to
   the child as an evidence commit naming H. H cannot contain a report naming
   its own future commit hash: preserve measured H versus evidence-head E and
   the evidence-only delta instead of inventing a self-referential SHA.
3. Lease one target directory exclusively. Prefer a new owned target per crate
   for the initial calibrated series; a borrowed cache is acceptable only with
   the owner releasing all Cargo/rust-analyzer writers and its provenance logged.
   No deletion of another target and no `cargo clean`. Shared registry downloads
   are distinct from compiled target/incremental cache and must be labelled.
4. Capture host OS/build, architecture, CPU/model/count, RAM, storage/runner image,
   UTC timestamp, rustc/cargo/clippy/fmt versions, explicit source SHA/tree,
   Cargo.lock/profile/toolchain hashes, selected crate/file/rank, target path,
   relevant environment and cache state. Capture names and allowlisted values,
   not tokens or a wholesale environment dump. No source change during a series.
5. Use process-local `QUANTICK_BUBBLES` pointing at the benchmark checkout's
   tracked `crates/app/config/bubbles.toml`; preserve the user's real config.
   Reject or explicitly normalize unrelated harness/update-schema variables.
   Pin command/profile/job-count choices once; do not secretly enable sccache,
   turn off incremental compilation, or change optimization for faster samples.
6. For each crate, run its exact timed command once as declared warm-up and
   record the full output/time separately. Then record one no-touch control.
   This is explicitly a warm-dependency incremental experiment, not cold build
   evidence. No-op controls are never reported as touched incremental samples.
7. Take five touched samples per crate, all retained. Save original byte hash,
   byte content recovery copy, permission/type and precise atime/mtime. Verify
   the path is a tracked, nonsymlink regular production file within the owned
   worktree and that current bytes still match H. Touch **mtime only**, after
   warm-up completes and beyond filesystem timestamp resolution; content stays
   identical to H. Use monotonic elapsed time around the full cargo process.
   Keep raw stdout/stderr and exit code, wall interval and touch metadata.
8. A valid touched sample must show the selected crate recompiling in Cargo's
   pinned output (`Compiling quantick-...`) and execute its tests successfully.
   If proof is ambiguous, use an explicitly recorded diagnostic invocation with
   Cargo structured compiler-artifact/fresh metadata outside the measured series;
   never accept an all-fresh/no-recompile sample as success. First implementation
   fixtures must prove the chosen observation method against the pinned Cargo.
9. In `finally`, verify source bytes still equal the expected H bytes before
   restoring timestamps. Never overwrite an unexpected concurrent edit: fail
   closed and retain recovery evidence/worktree. A content-changing fallback is
   not silently substituted for a timestamp touch. After the series, verify all
   original bytes and metadata, clean tracked/untracked state, same HEAD/lock,
   and that only one selected file was touched at a time. A killed process
   leaves a recovery manifest for the next owner; do not erase failed evidence.
10. Report every sample, median, range and maximum; do not select the fastest.
    Warm-up, controls, compile-only Cargo summary and end-to-end command wall
    time have separate fields. The latter is the edit-loop observation.

Cargo documents source mtime versus dep-info freshness checks, but that is an
implementation fact to verify under pinned Rust 1.98.0, not a license to infer
recompilation merely from editing a timestamp:
[Cargo fingerprint documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/nightly-rustc/cargo/core/compiler/fingerprint/index.html).

## Windows PR parity and scheduled budget defaults

C1 adds `read-cost` on Linux and its Python fixtures, with exact PR head/base
objects. It does not alter the existing `windows` job, which currently builds
the workspace, tests engine/guards and separately tests control-local. Preserve
C1's job/immutable-SHA artifact and Linux job unchanged. In the existing Windows
job add rustfmt/clippy component/version verification, then format, clippy,
build and full workspace test in that order. Retain the explicit named
control-local authority diagnostic step initially; full parity does not remove
its tested Windows ACL/transport paths. Keep job name `windows` to avoid an
unnecessary required-check rename. Keep bans/licenses enforced on Linux and the
separate advisory schedule; no change to dependency policy or toolchain pin.

Propose a separate `.github/workflows/edit-loop.yml`: weekly off-the-hour cron,
manual trigger and path-filtered PR trigger for this runner/workflow/budget and
relevant Cargo configuration. Use read-only permissions, GitHub-hosted Windows
(same runner family as parity), no credentials or self-hosted runner for PR code.
The same measurement/check command runs in every trigger. Upload raw artifacts
with `if: always()` and missing-output failure; job success cannot hide a failed
measurement/check. A process timeout produces retained partial failure output,
not zero milliseconds. No workflow-level continue-on-error or skip-as-pass.

Budget calibration must occur on the **scheduled runner's stated host class**,
not reuse desktop timings as a Windows-hosted-runner threshold. Commit per-crate
absolute budgets with raw initial five-sample baseline and rationale. Proposed
starting rule to review after real calibration: ceiling rounded upward from
`1.25 * max(valid baseline samples) + 5 seconds`, declared as operational noise
headroom, not a rubric threshold. Do not self-calibrate a passing budget from
each checked run. Record median/max and fail when a validated measured sample
exceeds the frozen budget. Major host/toolchain/top-three drift is explicit
uncalibrated failure requiring reviewed recalibration, not an automatic pass.
Keep the actual numbers unknown until measured; no invented latency promise.

Runner fixtures must cover rank selection/ties and excluded tests; wrong SHA or
dirty checkout; symlink/escaping/unowned paths; touch followed by no rebuild;
timeout/nonzero cargo; recovery after exception; unexpected byte changes during
restore; missing output/nonfinite/negative times; over-budget and host mismatch;
preserving every sample; and all-four Windows command ordering in the workflow.
Use injected clock/process/filesystem ports and fake Cargo fixtures so ordinary
tool tests never launch a real expensive build.

GitHub schedules run only from the default branch; adding a cron to a campaign
branch does not prove it ran. Exercise the identical budget job via the new PR
trigger before child delivery, retain that current-head evidence, and leave the
first default-branch cron observation explicitly pending for parent/main proof.
`workflow_dispatch` also initially requires default-branch presence, so it is
not the sole pre-merge test route. These are delivery facts, not settings tasks
or a reason to block implementation. See [GitHub trigger documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows).

## Genuine risks and bounded failure handling

- Shared targets are not isolated merely because Cargo serializes a lock:
  another worktree can change artifacts, feature unification and warm state.
  Root already recorded target disappearance during F1/R1; preserve that history.
  No unexplained cache miss/deletion is a passing incremental sample.
- Full-workspace warming is not equivalent to warming `cargo test -p crate`:
  app's `fake-native` dev feature and other resolution differences can rebuild
  package targets. Warm exactly the subsequently timed command per crate.
- The observed inherited personal bubble preset filtered quantity-one tests;
  this is a proven environment issue, not a flaky test to ignore. Keep original
  R1 failure/recovery evidence and explicit tracked fixture selection.
- Windows full tests may expose genuine ACL, filesystem, Python interpreter or
  socket timing failures Linux could not cover. Inspect actual failure logs;
  fix within C2 only where required for parity, coordinate other owners, and
  preserve assertions. Do not promise zero failures before running the new job.
- Hosted runner hardware/noisy neighbors and local app/build activity can
  contaminate timing. Record host load/concurrency, invalidate declared
  contaminated series without erasing it, and use bounded full-series reruns,
  not cherry-picking. Exclusive local lease includes dense GUI/perf work.
- If the campaign/main merge happens more than 30 days after measured H,
  remeasure the current relevant SHA; old child evidence is not fresh by decree.
- Optional settings task for parent, only if read-only inspection establishes
  it is missing: `Require the existing Windows CI check on protected main.`
  No settings write and no implementation wait; root owns that parent text.

## Dense-performance opportunities, explicitly not extra C2 acceptance

There are reusable current-source fixtures if root separately schedules a
bounded performance-evidence refresh; none measures Cargo edit-loop cost:

```text
cargo test -p quantick-app worker_progress_bench::dense_workers -- --ignored --exact --nocapture --test-threads=1
cargo test -p quantick-app app::tests::worker_summary_bench_tests::worker_summary_cadence_cost -- --ignored --exact --nocapture --test-threads=1
cargo test -p quantick-app app::tests::control_plane_tests::incremental_lane_dense_frame_benchmark -- --ignored --exact --nocapture --test-threads=1
cargo test -p quantick-app app::tests::control_plane_tests::control_idle_dense_replay_benchmark -- --ignored --exact --nocapture --test-threads=1
cargo test --release -p quantick-app live_envelope_tests::measure -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
```

The first emits Q8 worker data for time/dollar/depth with 30 warm-up and 600
measured bursts (`q8-dense-workers-v1`); the summary fixture emits
`q8-summary-cadence-v1`, 30/600 samples. Use tracked bubble config, exact SHA,
same profile/host, retained raw data and serialized baseline/candidate runs.
Do not add a hot-path rewrite, new benchmark family, production hook or score
claim to C2. If used only as optional current observations, label them separately
and do not let them postpone required parity/edit-loop delivery.

## Full retained source: issue #477 product clauses

> Reviewable outcome: ci(app): measure incremental edit loops and run full checks on Windows.
> Implement only this outcome under the parent's frozen measurement, independent assessment and invariant constraints. Source: authenticated user campaign request retained on parent, including the three explicit defect fixes and no ticket/replay regression. Parent estimates and PR claims are never success evidence.
> A1: Windows PR CI runs format, clippy, build and entire workspace test suite alongside Linux with pinned toolchain and dependency policy preserved.
> A2: Measure incremental cargo test -p crate after touching one production file in each of the three largest crates by frozen measure definition, on identified host; commit raw results and exact SHA less than 30 days old.
> A3: Scheduled job checks justified edit-loop budgets with failure evidence; no non-representative crate substitutions or silently warmed timings.
> A4: Current CI failures are diagnosed/fixed without weakening assertions or hiding historical flakes; settings changes remain one-line human tasks on parent.
> Owner class: autonomous. Priority: 4. Risk/tier: high. Estimated scope: one bounded outcome/PR (assessment B0 is evidence only). Dependencies: C1 integrated_campaign_with_green_ci (B0 uses accepted_evidence). Satisfaction requires reachable campaign merge SHA and exact-head green CI/reviews; issue closure alone is insufficient.
> Validation plan: Full loop, timing script fixtures and actual two-OS CI; measurements occur in isolated worktree with original content restored safely.
